newsitem.title: USA: Gore fills in for Clinton in weekly radio address.
newsitem.headline: Gore fills in for Clinton in weekly radio address.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore served as President Clinton's substitute Saturday in delivering a radio address that called for $5 billion in federal aid to public schools in need of repair.
"The president's doing great," Gore said, referring to Clinton's operation on Friday to repair a torn tendon. "He's resting comfortably and he'll be back on his feet, both of them, very soon."
Promoting the need to provide quality education across the nation, Gore warned that "in an age of tight budgets, we should be spending public funds on teachers and children."
He lamented that "many or our schoolhouses are now at an all-time low -- rundown, overcrowded, and stuck with ancient technology or no technology at all."
He called for support for Clinton's call for $5 billion in federal aid to help the financially strapped school system -- a proposal that was formally submitted to Congress on Friday.
"We simply cannot ask our teachers to build up children in buildings that are literally falling down," Gore said.
